Front door

Denver onboarding

A web flow from a friend’s invite link that skips the normal Benable sign-up: connect once to bring your places in, pick your Top 5, land in Ask Denver.

Why

  • Sign-up today is about 20 screens built for creators and brand deals. Nothing asks about Denver.Mobile app, Nov 18
  • People arrive with their places, not an empty profile: 209 Denver places found in 36 creators’ posts.Research sheet, Nov 20
  • Invites are the growth engine: over 80% of Beli’s users joined through a referral.Ivey Business Review
  • On the web, so it needs no app release before Dec 11.

First stepAmbassadors’ invite links before the Dec 2 dinner.

Denver onboarding · why

Every new Denver person should arrive with places, not an empty profile

The problem today
  • Sign-up is about 20 screens built for creators and brand deals. Nothing asks about Denver.Mobile app, Nov 18
  • Asked to add a rec cold, people forget everything they love.Olivia, Nov 6
Why people would use it
  • Connect once and we find the places already in their posts. No sharing posts one by one.
  • A friend’s invite with her Top 5 is a reason to join, not a form.
Why it matters for Benable
  • Ambassador invites are the growth engine: over 80% of Beli’s users joined through a referral.Ivey Business Review
  • 209 places already found in 36 Denver creators’ posts, so profiles start full.Research sheet, Nov 20
  • It runs on the web and bypasses the normal onboarding, like the quick onboarding we built for creators, so it needs no app release before Dec 11.
How we’d know it works
  • Share of Denver sign-ups who keep 5 or more places and finish a Top 5 in their first session.
  • Invites sent per ambassador, and how many turn into sign-ups.

A web flow from the invite link that bypasses the normal onboarding, like the quick creator one. Ambassadors get a badge.

Onboarding · options we’re weighing

How do recs come in?

Connect once and get your places back; Google Maps lists and screenshots as other ways in.

Why it’s worth it

  • Our creator onboarding already connects Instagram and TikTok and gets posts with captions: 25 latest Instagram posts, a year of TikToks.Benable code today
  • Those captions are already stored for every creator who connected, so we can find their places without asking again.Benable code today
  • Research found 209 Denver places in 36 creators’ posts. Sharing posts one by one wouldn’t get people there.Research sheet, Nov 20

The catchInstagram only connects creator or business accounts, and captions have no location tag, so places come from reading the text. Reusing stored captions may need a line of consent.

Smallest way to try itFind places in the captions we already store for creators who connected, and send them their list.

Denver Top 5 · why

Five slots turn a long list into a point of view

The problem today
  • Profiles are long lists. Nothing says who you are at a glance, or whose taste to trust.
  • A new Denver user has no quick way to introduce themselves.
Why people would use it
  • Curation is identity: Letterboxd’s four favorites and StoryGraph’s shelf are the most-shared part of the profile.The Spinoff, Apr 2025
  • Five slots make each pick mean something, and say what kind of Denver local you are.Olivia’s proposal
Why it matters for Benable
  • An easy first assignment for every ambassador, and a beautiful thing to post: every Story card is an invite.
  • The star on a place carries endorsements into discovery and shared tastes.
How we’d know it works
  • Share of Denver profiles with all five filled.
  • Story shares of the card, and follows that start from a Top 5.

Five places that say who you are

All five the same size, each with a short reason, on every Denver profile. A restaurant and a thrift shop can’t be ranked against each other.

When someone else picked the same place, show the person, their note, and a way to follow.

Ask Denver · why

The moment you need somewhere to go, Benable should be the app you open

The problem today
  • When you need a place tonight, you text friends or post a Story, and the answers get lost in the thread.Olivia, Nov 6
  • Benable has no reason to be opened in that moment: it’s lists, not answers.
Why people would use it
  • Hyper-specific asks get answers from real locals, saved with the exact tip.Olivia’s proposal
  • Crumbs of NYC, a Substack chat, has 8,000+ subscribers and answered an ask every day of 2025.Crumbs of NYC
Why it matters for Benable
  • It’s our goal in one feature: open Benable when you need somewhere to go.
  • Every answer is a rec, so asking creates content, and people start recognizing whose taste they trust.
How we’d know it works
  • Half of asks come in without a nudge by week two.
  • The first answer lands inside an hour, and one in three asks ends with a save.

How people get closer

Six small steps from a stranger’s rec to someone you trust

1eyeSee

You notice someone’s rec: an answer in Ask Denver, a place in their Top 5, a shared taste.

You getA name attached to a place, not an algorithm.
They getNothing yet.
2bookmarkSave

You save their place to Want to Try.

You getA plan, with their tip kept on it.
They get“Maya saved your rec.”
3thumbAgree

Thumbs-up their answer, or you both have it in your Top 5.

You getA quick way to say “same”.
They getTheir answer rises for others.
4userFollow

We suggest it when it’s earned: after a shared taste, a useful answer, or your third save of their places.

You getTheir new places on your home.
They getA follower who chose them for a reason.
5heartGo and thank

You tried their place and say thanks in your own words.

You getA place that turned out right.
They get“Ava went because of you.” The strongest moment.
6sparkTwins

We notice you agree on most places and give you a name, like Vintage Besties.

You getThe person to watch, with a heads-up when they add a place.
They getA fan, and a reason to keep adding.

Each step is something people already want to do. Benable just notices, and makes the next one easy. One-way follows, like Instagram; nobody has to accept.

How people get closer · why

Getting closer is what makes every other feature better

What it’s useful for
  • Home: places from people whose taste you share come first, instead of whatever’s trending.
  • Ask Denver: answers from people like you show first, and the nudge goes to people whose recs fit.
  • A newcomer with no follows still gets the ambassadors, so home is never empty.
How we nudge each step
  • Suggest a follow at the moment it’s earned (a shared taste, a great answer, the third save), never a follow-all list.Nov 20 call
  • Small social lines everywhere: “Maya wants to try it too”, “In Jules’s Top 5”.
  • Twins and pairing names make the closest match feel special and worth sharing.
Why people keep giving
  • Recognition when their recs are saved, tried or thanked, in the other person’s words.
  • A visible Top 5 star and followers who came for a reason.
  • For ambassadors: their influence on Denver, made visible.
What’s already built, what’s open
  • Follows, contact matching and suggested follows already exist in the backend.Benable code today
  • Open: does a twin show up for both people, or only to you? Can a twin be turned off?
  • Open: which signal counts most for home, follows or taste overlap?

Appendix · other ideas

Fourteen more, roughly ranked

1. Customize your list coverPick photos, a type style, colors from your photos and stickers for any list’s cover.
2. Customize your profileA background with soft pastel shapes, a palette and an accent for your profile.
3. Taste match, as a storyInvite someone to a match: your % match, the place that brings you together, then three of their places you’d like.
4. Taste twinsYour closest match gets a name (Vintage Besties) and a spot on home; when they add a place, you hear about it in one short notification.
5. A mini guide for one personSomeone asks for something specific; Benable pulls 3 to 5 of your own places into a private guide with your notes, ready to text.
6. Recognition loopsTell people when their recs get saved or tried, in the other person’s words: a notification when it happens, a recap on Sunday.
7. A public Want to Try listSaving a place offers a To try list you can make public, with save counts.
8. Social proof on a recShow how many people saved a rec and how many profiles it’s on.
9. Sending a recPick a friend, add a line in your own words, and they get a card with your note and one tap to save it, app or not.
10. My People MapA map of the places your people recommend, with their faces on it.
11. Events in Ask DenverAnswer an ask with an event, and see what’s on in Denver this week.
12. List ideas after your Top 5Right after your Top 5, Benable suggests lists from what you just added: “You added Sexy Pizza. Best pizza in Denver?”
13. Answer from a Story linkAmbassadors post an ask to their Instagram Story; followers tap “Answer on Benable” and answer on the web, no app needed.
14. A weekly prompt (parked)One prompt a week for all of Denver; share yours to see everyone’s.

Each can join a future ambassador program: carry Denver’s features over and add one new idea each time.

A mini guide for one person

Someone asks for something specific; Benable pulls 3 to 5 of your own places into a private guide with your notes, ready to text.

Why it could work

  • Olivia’s idea: “create a mini guide of all the places in this list that someone could go shop for a gift at”, then send it by text.Olivia, Nov 4
  • AI on the recommender’s side, not the seeker’s: packaging a custom answer is what takes time today.Julia, Nov 4
  • Lists assume a wide audience; a guide made for your mom says “for you”, and every guide sent is an invite.

Appendix · 9 of 14

Sending a rec

Pick a friend, add a line in your own words, and they get a card with your note and one tap to save it, app or not.

Why it could work

  • Today, Share offers an Instagram Story or the phone’s share sheet with a bare link. No friend picker, no note, and you never hear what happened.Benable code today
  • The person you send to sees your note and the place, and saves it to Want to Try in one tap, even without the app.
  • Every send carries your invite code and comes back to you as “Theo saved it”, so sending turns into growth and recognition.
Smallest way to try itAdd a note field and a recent-people row to today’s share sheet.

One more · the map

A Denver map made of people

We explored the Benable map on Nov 3: Benable’s colors on the map, and people and asks as the pins.

Why

  • Most new places come from a friend: Snap reports 65% of new-place visits follow one.Snap, reported
  • Snap Map started testing “visited and recommended” tags from creators in Jul 2026, close to our idea.Snap, Jul 2026
  • Ask Denver answers already have places, so a map view comes almost for free.

The catchThe colored map needs a map library we can style (Mapbox or MapLibre). Faces, asks and overlays work on any map.

Your readA map view inside Ask Denver first, or its own tab after Dec 11?
